A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ExPLAIND, its kernel equivalence, pruning validation and modulo-addition Grokking study. The text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original kernel-validation, pruning, Grokking, layer-swapping, retraining and Lasso results in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: V2 retains original kernel-validation and pruning results in Sections 3–4 and Grokking experiments and analyses in Section 5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The core optimizer-aware attribution and pruning procedures remain. However, v2 Definition 4.4 generalizes similarity to flattened influence tensors, whereas v1 Equations 5–6 compare parameter vectors accumulated over training samples and steps. This changes the specified score construction; the PDFs do not establish recomputation of the retained experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-2 cat/dog classification and MOD-113 addition, including the same checkpoint-swapping and reinitialization scenarios. The new loss/intermediate-activation corollary has no accompanying evaluation on additional tasks.

E2.justification: The pruning comparison retains Li et al. (2017) and Random in v1 Figure 1 and v2 Figure 2. Kernel validation still compares the reformulation against the original models. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The similarity statistic for geometric analysis is reformulated from accumulated parameter vectors to flattened tensor slices (v1 Equation 6; v2 Equation 8). This is a reported metric-definition revision, without evidence of rerunning the analysis. Appendix C's splits, architectures and training settings, and the accuracy/KL and 10/100-integration-step evaluations otherwise match.

E4.justification: Integration-step sensitivity, layer swapping, confusion-matrix analysis, checkpoint reinitialization and Lasso analysis are retained after matching Appendix E. V2 omits the training/test-loss and weight-decay trajectory panels from v1 Figure 2, reducing the training-dynamics diagnostics. The relocated intervention plots are not new ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run means and standard deviations for pruning and pipeline-reinitialization experiments. V2 removes v1's explicit limitation that the complete analysis could not be confirmed across multiple training runs. This removes replication information without establishing that additional independent Grokking runs occurred.

E6.justification: V2 omits v1 Figure 2's visible loss and weight-decay trajectories and narrows the pruning finding from outperforming the baseline at 70–99% sparsity to performing competitively. The displayed pruning curves, kernel-validation values, intervention outcomes and all nine nonzero Lasso coefficients remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds Corollary 3.3 and its proof for loss and intermediate-activation decompositions. It substantively revises the central AdamW formulas, including loss derivatives, learning-rate/regularization factors and historical mini-batch membership, and revises similarity and regularization definitions. Appendix D.1 adds a derivation of constant loss gradients for log-probability outputs and changes the stated kernel-machine conditions. The momentum derivation already existed in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: extending EPK to realistic optimizers, unifying model/data/training attribution, validating influence through pruning, and identifying embedding-decoder alignment in Grokking. The rewritten contribution list changes emphasis and organization rather than these claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the retained reinitialization experiment as confirming causal alignment and layer swapping as changing the prediction algorithm to use cyclic representations. It adds the limitation that insights are qualitative and not automated, removes the multiple-training-run caveat and vocabulary-alignment fine-tuning extrapolation, and expands scalability discussion.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly specifies final log-softmax outputs in Appendix D.1, adds early-accumulation and subsampling guidance in Section 4.1, and discloses LLM assistance with coding. Appendix C's hyperparameters, hardware and compute totals, and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds the CIFAR-10 dataset citation and removes Bell (2024), dataset-cartography/training-trajectory discussion, and the Geva/Han vocabulary-alignment connection. Most cited research remains, including material moved to Appendix B. Bibliographic updates and Wang's preprint/publication variants do not constitute distinct new research coverage.

P1.justification: The introduction, framework exposition and Grokking narrative are extensively rewritten. Theory and validation are separated from framework/pruning sections; Grokking is reorganized into influence decomposition and cyclic geometry. Related work moves partly to Appendix B, ethical sections merge, and reproducibility and LLM-use statements are added. Title and author information also change.

P2.justification: V2 adds a framework schematic, splits the original validation composite into Table 1 and Figure 2, and assembles training and retained reinitialization plots into Figure 3. Layer-swapping plots move to Appendix Figure 7; Lasso graphics and coefficients become separate displays. Main-text heatmap selections shrink while full appendix versions remain, with extensive caption and layout revisions.

improvement.justification: V2 improves navigation and makes parts of the derivation more explicit. However, Definition 4.3 uses signed influences while describing absolute-influence differences, and the paper removes the explicit replication caveat while strengthening causal language without additional empirical support. These presentation and clarification gains coexist with mathematical and reporting concerns, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
